newsitem.title: FRANCE: Cerus up on expected offer for Valeo stake.
newsitem.headline: Cerus up on expected offer for Valeo stake.

text.p: French holding company Cerus was up by 5.65 percent in mid-afternoon on Friday at 131.0 francs after another French holding company CGIP said it was ready to buy its 28 percent stake in car parts maker Valeo.
CGIP was down 2.55 percent at 1,185 francs.
Cerus is the French holding company of Italian businessman Carlo de Benedetti who has been looking for a buyer for his Valeo stock for nearly a year.

CGIP announced late Thursday it would sell half of its 20 percent stake in packaging group Crown Cork & Seal Co to finance the purchase of the Valeo stake from the Cerus company and to balance out its holdings.
Valeo was up 1.25 percent at 282.4 francs.
The Paris government and French car manufacturers have been trying to arrange a French purchase of the stake to fend off a buyout bid by U.S.- or other foreign competitors.
CGIP has said its board wants to conclude a deal but it has not disclosed terms.
